data: Artur Sogomonyan is an AI Engineer based in Vienna, Austria. His background spans applied machine learning, computer vision, 3D geometry and toolpath software for multi-axis manufacturing, full-stack development, and hands-on making.
What does Artur Sogomonyan work on?

Artur Sogomonyan works where models meet products: shaping the data, testing the method, building the service, and making the result understandable to the person using it. His work covers applied machine learning, computer vision, 3D geometry and toolpath software for multi-axis manufacturing, LLM and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, and full-stack web development.

Artur Sogomonyan’s education includes an MSc Data Science at Technische Universität Wien (TU Wien, 2022–2026) and a BSc Information Technologies and Telecommunications at Bauman Moscow State Technical University (2014–2020), where his diploma thesis was a 3D-printer failure-detection system based on computer vision. He also attended Deep Learning School (MIPT, 2020–2021) and School of Data Analysis (HSE & Yandex, 2020).
Which languages does Artur Sogomonyan speak?
Artur Sogomonyan speaks English (C1), Russian (C2), Armenian (B2), and German (A2), with levels given on the CEFR scale.
What is Artur Sogomonyan’s work experience?

Artur Sogomonyan currently works at Flexam on software for industrial multi-axis additive manufacturing: 3D segmentation, slicing, toolpath and G-code generation for robot arms and multi-axis machines, and the full-stack slicer product in Go, Rust, Python, and TypeScript. Artur Sogomonyan’s earlier roles include CTO & Data Scientist at susteam, Jan 2023 – Feb 2025; Research Scientist at TU Wien (Rail4Future), Feb – Jul 2024; and Machine Learning Analyst at GLOSAV, Feb – Jul 2021. Before that, he worked on 3D modelling and prototyping as well as frontend and full-stack web development.
Which technologies does Artur Sogomonyan use?

Artur Sogomonyan’s toolkit covers machine learning & vision (PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, OpenCV, YOLO), language & retrieval (NLP, LLMs, RAG, LangChain), software engineering (Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, C++, Node.js, Bun, Svelte, React, three.js, FastAPI, Docker), 3D & manufacturing (3D segmentation, mesh processing, slicing, toolpath generation, G-code, robot arms, multi-axis printing, trimesh), and data & infrastructure (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, AWS, Linux, nginx, Git, CI/CD).
Does Artur Sogomonyan work with LLMs and RAG?

Yes. Artur Sogomonyan built an ESG analytics platform (susteam) that combined OCR with retrieval-augmented language models to automate sustainability reporting, and his AIM Hackathon project, which placed 2nd, used RAG to detect greenwashing in corporate ESG reports.
What computer-vision work has Artur Sogomonyan done?

Artur Sogomonyan worked on real-time computer vision for railway-route and obstacle detection at GLOSAV, and his diploma thesis at Bauman Moscow State Technical University was a 3D-printer failure-detection system based on computer vision.
Which projects best show Artur Sogomonyan’s work?
The featured projects on Artur Sogomonyan’s site are Flexam, susteam, Rail4Future, GLOSAV, and Web development path. Each has its own page with context, approach, and stack.
What awards and publications does Artur Sogomonyan have?

Artur Sogomonyan took 1st place at the AI Mission Hackathon 3 (Oct 2025; team “Nightwalkers” — a multi-tool AI agent that autonomously answered complex sustainability questions, reaching over 70% accuracy on database and Wikipedia queries); 2nd place at the AIM Hackathon (Oct 2024; hosted by TIMETOACT Group — RAG for greenwashing detection); and 2nd place at the Tourism Technology Hackathon (Nov 2023; tourism knowledge graph with an interactive map). He also co-authored “Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning-based Surrogate Modeling Approaches for Multi-body Dynamic Simulation in Railway Digital Twin Platform”, published in the proceedings of the 2024 IEEE International Conference on Industrial Engineering and Engineering Management (IEEM), pages 1074–1078 (DOI 10.1109/IEEM62345.2024.10857013).
What kinds of problems is Artur Sogomonyan a good fit for?

Artur Sogomonyan is most useful on ambiguous work: incomplete data, a model that needs a real product around it, or a prototype that has to become dependable. Typical examples are applied-AI products, computer-vision pipelines, and systems that need both model and interface thinking.
Where can I download Artur Sogomonyan’s CV?

Artur Sogomonyan’s CV is available as a PDF at https://github.com/PropovedNik007/cv/raw/main/Artur_Sogomonyan_cv_long.pdf. The About page summarises the same experience, education, skills, and languages.
How can I contact Artur Sogomonyan?

You can reach Artur Sogomonyan by email at arthur.sogomonyan@gmail.com, on LinkedIn (linkedin.com/in/artur-sogomonyan), on Telegram (t.me/arterrai), or on GitHub (github.com/PropovedNik007); he also writes on Medium (medium.com/@artur.sogomonyan). A useful first message names the outcome you want, the current constraint, and the next decision.
What else is on Artur Sogomonyan’s site besides projects?

Besides projects, the site has DIY build notes; sport notes on hiking, boxing, diving, and table tennis; and an Insights page with an interactive knowledge graph that connects the notes, a chart of how projects flow through fields of work, a self-assessed skills profile, and public GitHub activity plus anonymised totals from private organisation work.
